title: Music Nerd API
description: Artist profiles, research and onboarding, behind Music Nerd and open to other clients.
body:
The Music Nerd API serves the data behind [Music Nerd](https://www.musicnerd.xyz) and runs the research that builds an artist's profile: finding their profiles, reading what's written about them, and writing their Lore and About.

Base URL: `https://musicnerd-api.vercel.app`

Every reference page has a **Try it** panel that sends the request from your browser and shows the live response.

<CardGroup cols="2">
  <Card title="Quickstart" href="/quickstart">Make your first request in under a minute.</Card>
  <Card title="Authentication" href="/authentication">Which endpoints are public, and how to sign the rest.</Card>
  <Card title="API reference" href="/api-reference">Every endpoint, its request and its responses.</Card>
  <Card title="For AI tools" href="/llms.txt">The whole site as Markdown: `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`.</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Conventions

- Responses are flat JSON: `{ "status": "ok", ... }` on success and `{ "status": "error", "error": "<message>" }` on failure. There is no `data` wrapper.
- Every endpoint answers CORS preflight, so a browser on any origin can call it.
- Artist and account IDs are UUIDs. The same artist has a different ID in staging and production.

title: Quickstart
description: Make your first request to the Music Nerd API.
body:
## Check the API is up

The health endpoint needs no credentials:

```bash
curl https://musicnerd-api.vercel.app/api/health
```

```json
{ "status": "ok" }
```

## Call an endpoint for an artist

Endpoints that change an artist need the artist's claimant (or an admin) signed in. Music Nerd signs requests with the user's Privy access token, sent as a Bearer token:

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://musicnerd-api.vercel.app/api/artist/YOUR_ARTIST_ID/research/refresh \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_PRIVY_ACCESS_TOKEN'
```

See [Authentication](/authentication) for where that token comes from.

<Tip>Every reference page has a **Try it** panel. Paste a token once and it is kept in that browser tab until you close it.</Tip>

title: Authentication
description: Public endpoints, Privy access tokens, and the scheduler secret.
body:
Each endpoint's reference page states which of these it needs.

## Public

Read-only endpoints that expose nothing private need no credentials. Endpoints are public unless they return private data or change something.

## Privy access token

Endpoints that change an artist need the artist's approved claimant or a Music Nerd admin. Send the user's [Privy](https://www.privy.io) access token:

```bash
--header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_PRIVY_ACCESS_TOKEN'
```

In the Music Nerd web app the token comes from Privy's `getAccessToken()`. Tokens expire after about an hour; fetch a fresh one for each request.

| Response | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `400` `artistId must be a UUID` | The artist ID in the path is malformed. |
| `401` `Not signed in` | No token, an invalid or expired token, or no Music Nerd user for it. |
| `403` `Not your artist` | The user is neither the artist's claimant nor an admin. |

## Scheduler secret

`GET /api/research/advance` is the research scheduler that Vercel Cron calls. When the deployment sets `CRON_SECRET`, it requires `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`.
